source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #378 (branch fix/194-continuation-bridge at head 1d4529f085dc0dc925278af96386c42da7294f3d — the #194 change (the default memory’s local atomic load/store/RMW/cmpxchg handlers — 63 handlers — lowered natively in the shared baseline JIT instead of crossing the current-op continuation bridge) merged with current main 79d48f99226ca062ef62b42fcd3e9bed66d7c327 (PR #374), plus an integration commit allowing clippy::too_many_arguments on the 64-bit cmpxchg lowering helper, a size-gate re-baseline, and a follow-up fix widening the memarg offset to u64 before adding the i64 atomic load high-half displacement (Codex P2 on the PR); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45768617733, 45768630162 and 45768642576 against the branch produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Second re-baseline for PR #378 (#194, native baseline-JIT lowerings for the default memory’s local atomic load/store/RMW/cmpxchg handlers), following the Codex P2 fix that widens the memarg offset to u64 before adding the i64 atomic load high-half displacement in atomic_load64_half (commit 1d4529f085dc0dc925278af96386c42da7294f3d, on top of the first re-baseline at 30469ed). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45768655143, 45768668228 and 45768680439 on main at 79d48f99226ca062ef62b42fcd3e9bed66d7c327 (PR #374); all three runs pass the gate; the main control is byte-identical to the checked-in baseline on the sixteen series of the baseline, core, core-nosimd and core-aot configurations, measures below it on the core-jit series by exactly this PR’s delta (12,208 B / 8,608 B in release and 5,584 B / 4,112 B in release-size), and measures well below the retained baselines on the twelve series of the three configurations that link telomere-component). This PR’s own delta against the main control remains confined to the core-jit configuration: in release, stripped file +12,208 B and stripped .text +8,608 B (unchanged by the fix); in release-size, stripped file +5,600 B and stripped .text +4,128 B — the +16 B on each release-size series against the first re-baseline is the widened displacement computation in the telomere library, which only the core-jit configuration links with the jit feature. Every other series is byte-identical to main in both profiles. Against the checked-in baseline only the two release-size core-jit series grow (+16 B each), so only those two series are re-baselined to the branch measurements and every other baseline is retained, following the established practice of re-baselining growth only. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the three branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release component stripped file series at +11.42% (2,433,656 B to 2,711,648 B), unchanged because that series’ baseline is retained. The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
